clue.text: Composed a line and had American musicians play

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the words around 'and' are rearranged

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a line of verse and got some American musicians to perform it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' rearranges A LINE and HAD into ANIDEALH; 'and' just joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's comedy of 1895 is one example of a stage play.

clue.text: Spinning plate with dotty, funny picture

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the word for plate is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer
crackers is slang for mad or dotty

explanation.surface: A spinning plate, perhaps in a circus, accompanies a daft and comical image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a film: this is a Marx Brothers comedy, and 'Spinning' turns the plate word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brothers comedy of 1930 is a film, and a funny picture is a comic movie.

clue.text: Native Americans journalist's covered

parts.note: the Incas were the native people of Peru
ED, an editor, is the crossword journalist; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A journalist has written up a story about Native Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered' looks like a reporter covering a story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something encased has been wrapped or enclosed, a synonym of covered.

clue.text: Genesis or Kinks making an appearance

indicators.note: kinks are twists and bends, so the letters of the two words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Two rock bands, Genesis or the Kinks, turn up on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis and the Kinks look like a pair of bands; Kinks is the anagram signal and only GENESIS OR is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of coming or going out, so emerging into view.

clue.text: Want to pen new book to reminisce

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a pen for animals, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: want in the sense of lack, need

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of book

explanation.surface: Someone wishing to write a new book in order to recall the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing the book, but 'to pen' means to enclose; 'new' scrambles the book.
explanation.definitionFit: To look back is an idiom for thinking about past events, the same as to reminisce.

clue.text: Not firm catching a throw

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the single letter goes within the other word

parts.note: a jelly that has not set is unset, not firm

explanation.surface: Someone unsteady fumbles while trying to catch a thrown ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like a noun after 'a', but it is a verb, as a horse throws its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that throws its rider removes them from the saddle, which is to unseat them.

clue.text: Again touring empty apartments' grounds

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: bis is the musical direction meaning again, repeat

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Revisiting the grounds of some vacant flats.
explanation.walkthrough: Bis is a musical instruction to repeat a passage; 'empty' keeps only the ends of apartments, and 'touring' wraps the repeat word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds for an argument are its basis, its underlying foundation.

clue.text: Fledgling cuckoo can nest

indicators.note: cuckoo means mad, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A young cuckoo, just fledged, manages to build a nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like the bird in a nesting scene but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fledgling enterprise is newly begun, which is what nascent describes.

clue.text: Academic failing to turn up entertaining prospect

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the chance goes inside

parts.note: a failing is a moral fault or vice

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to roll is to turn over
a prospect of something happening is a chance

explanation.surface: A lecturer fails to show up despite the promise of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses the word for turn, and the failing plus that reversal entertain the prospect where the two meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's chief executive officer is an academic title holder.

clue.text: Acquire debts interest-free

parts.note: to incur is to bring upon oneself or acquire, usually a cost
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Run up debts on a loan that charges no interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest-free' looks like a loan term; here it means showing no curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: An incurious person lacks curiosity, so is free of interest in things.

clue.text: The Guardian plugs reduced transport fare from the East

indicators.note: plugs means fills a gap, so this pair goes inside
reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to ship goods is to transport them
the newspaper speaking of itself says us

explanation.surface: The newspaper fills its pages with stories about cheaper fares on transport from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price but is food; 'reduced' cuts SHIP to SHI, which US goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish, so food from the Far East.

clue.text: Nincompoops, many losing face

indicators.note: losing face means the word drops its front letter

parts.note: masses means a great many

explanation.surface: Fools, a great number of them, suffer public humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses is a common term of abuse for foolish people, like nincompoops.

clue.text: Bolder men stripped off clothing

parts.note: brassy means bold, so bolder is brassier

indicators.note: stripped off means the outer letters are peeled away, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Some brazen men have taken their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped off' leaves the middle letter of men, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is an item of underwear, and so of clothing.

clue.text: Man put on sham cover for crown jewels

indicators.note: put on means placed after in an across entry, so the piece follows

parts.note: cod is slang for mock or sham, as in cod Latin
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A man puts on a fake covering for the royal regalia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown jewels' is slang for a man's genitals, not the royal regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: The pouch worn on the front of Tudor breeches covered the groin, jokily called the crown jewels.

clue.text: Shock time to emerge

parts.note: chicks hatch, emerging from the egg

explanation.surface: Surprise: the moment has come to come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like surprise but is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A thatch of hair is a thick mop of it, just as a shock of hair is.

clue.text: One raises issue about breaking smashed lock

indicators.note: breaking means splitting apart, so the letter goes into the middle

parts.note: smashed and high are both slang for intoxicated
a lock is a strand of hair
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a matter of a broken, damaged lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring, so one that raises issue is a seat that lifts a child up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat lifts a baby or toddler up to table height, raising one's offspring.

clue.text: Officer and staff oppressing revolutionary native Americans

indicators.note: oppressing means weighing down on, so in a down entry these come above

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
to man is to staff, as a station
Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: An officer and his team crack down on a rebel group of indigenous people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains.

clue.text: A queen accepts Meghan's No 1 fashion icon

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the letter goes inside the queen

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of Meghan

explanation.surface: A queen welcomes the Duchess of Sussex's favourite style leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, is a noted style figure; only her initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is an Italian designer, an example of a fashion icon.

clue.text: Token internet phenomenon not funny

parts.note: a meme is an idea or image that spreads online

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of the word are shuffled

explanation.surface: A symbolic internet craze that fails to be amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake or souvenir, a token of remembrance.

clue.text: Kind of stock car feature with pine at the front

indicators.note: at the front means this piece is placed first

parts.note: to pine for is to long for
a horn is a fitting on a car

explanation.surface: A stock car fitted with something made of pine at its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' is livestock, not the car or shares; 'pine' is the verb, not the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Longhorns are a breed of cattle, and so a kind of livestock.

clue.text: Setting a goal? It's a pain

indicators.note: setting means arranging in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aiming for a target is a chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' rearranges A GOAL and IT; the 's is 'is', joining the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical term for earache, a specific kind of pain.

clue.text: Make an effort in special school

parts.note: to school is to train or teach

explanation.surface: Try hard at a school for children with special needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is the verb, to coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to exert oneself greatly, to make an effort.

clue.text: A rum task involved a sensual work

indicators.note: involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An odd job turns out to be a sexual activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges A RUM TASK, and the second 'a' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Sanskrit text on love and pleasure is a work on sensual matters.

clue.text: Rush in rising river banks in Powys

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means reading upwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales and England

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A torrent rushing into a river in flood along the banks in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Powys is a county in Wales; 'banks in' keeps P and S, and 'rising' turns DEEPS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to go fast, so speed is a synonym.

clue.text: Caught London gangsters making crack

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard or picked up by ear, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the Kray twins ran organised crime in London's East End in the 1960s

explanation.surface: A police catch of East End villains leads to a breakthrough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' wants to be C, the cricket abbreviation, leaving RAZE for the gangsters; nothing fits, as it signals hearing. The Krays were notorious London gangster twins.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a network of fine cracks in a glaze or varnish, so to craze is to crack.

clue.text: Sierra raced outside of Grenoble

parts.note: ran is the past of run, so raced

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Ford Sierra car sped around the outskirts of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' looks like the car, but means a mountain chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a chain of jagged mountains, a mountain range.

clue.text: Lord's helper needs a switch between sides

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle of the sides

parts.note: R and L are right and left, the two sides
a switch is a change

explanation.surface: A Lord's cricketing assistant needs to switch ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' looks like the cricket ground or a peer; it means God.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is a senior angel, a servant of God.

clue.text: Capital radio's bum tune

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the next word is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: bum is British slang for the backside, the derriere

explanation.surface: A London radio station plays a terrible song.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital Radio is a London station; 'bum' looks like an adjective meaning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish melody, also used for Danny Boy, is a well-known tune.
